_comment: The exceptions to installing the Eunoia ecosystem, and nothing else.
What to clone is derived from tools/ecosystem.json: every entry there that
is not a child project carries a url and a repo id, and the clone follows
from them. A tool added to the inventory therefore appears in the dump, in
the status view and in scripts/repos.local without anybody editing this
file -- which is the point, because a second list to maintain is a second
list to forget.
**Only a default branch is ever installed.** scripts/install_eo prints and
runs `git clone <url> <dir>` and nothing else: no `-b`, no checkout, no
branch switch. Where a child project's current work is on some other
branch of its parent -- ethos-eoc, on ethosEoc3 -- that is a fact about
the child and is recorded on the child, in tools/ecosystem.json. The
parent still installs, and the install says which branch to go to for the
newest copy of the child.
So this file holds only what cannot be derived. Keyed by repo id:
args         extra clone flags, with the reason in `why`
opt_in       why this one is not cloned by default. Its command is
printed commented out and `--run` skips it unless it is named
why          what a reader needs that the inventory's `what` does not say
url          only for a repo the inventory does not carry. The status
view reports that as a status somebody still owes
`order` is the order of the dump. Anything unlisted follows, inventory
order within its status, so a new tool lands in a sensible place unasked.

anoieu.why: where this list lives, so you already have it if you are reading this

ethos.why: the proof checker's own tree. Its `main` is what the Eunoia manual is read from and what findings against the checker are measured against; the ethos-eoc child project lives here too

cvc5.why: nothing here builds it and only proofs/eo is read, so the blobless clone is the whole of what is wanted -- drop the filter if you intend to build it
cvc5.opt_in: the largest tree here by an order of magnitude, and nothing needs a working copy of it: tools/deps.py fetches proofs/eo shallow and sparse when a report is generated
